human_review: Payouts check
A bookkeeper confirms each unpaid, short or doubled payout against the marketplace or processor statement and sends any inquiry; a person reviews and posts each settlement journal entry.
Marketplace money back
A person checks each FBA claim, storage fee and fee dispute against Seller Central before filing it, and writes and submits every claim response; nothing is filed or answered by the agents.
Returns and promotions

Customer service decides each refund, chase and reminder; a manager decides what to do about a discount code or a repeat returner; finance confirms gift card liability and every affiliate reversal before payout.
Sales tax pack
Your tax adviser confirms the rates, registrations and thresholds in the settings and decides every filing and registration; the agents only compare and draft a worksheet.
Inventory and listings
A merchandiser decides each listing, price, reorder and ad change in the channel itself; the agents never change a listing, price, budget or purchase order.
Shipping and purchasing
Someone in operations disputes carrier, 3PL and retailer charges in each portal, approves supplier invoices and updates product costs; drafts are sent only by a person.
Store cash and shrink
A store manager talks through each drawer shortage and missing deposit with the staff involved and decides on any recount; shrink figures are for the manager, not for staff records.
Whole shop
Every finding in every pack goes to a named person, who looks and acts; the agents only read files and write reports and drafts.
Multi-brand business
Each brand or account owner reviews their own findings, and settings (fees, tax, thresholds) are confirmed separately for each one.
Partner rollout
The firm's staff review each client's findings and confirm each client's settings with that client before acting on anything.
common_problems: Orders never paid out or paid short by a marketplace (an Amazon order paid 2.00 short in the demo week).
Fees above your schedule: a 20% referral charged on a home item, a fulfilment fee 0.88 above the fixed amount.
FBA units lost in the warehouse and never reimbursed, and refunds whose return never came back, each with a claim-by date.
Refunds paid twice or above the price, and items received back that were never refunded.
Affiliate commission paid on refunded orders, or at a rate above your terms.
Listings that can oversell what the warehouse can ship, and stock sitting on a shelf with no live listing.
Shipping labels costing more than the customer was charged, and voided labels never refunded.
Retailer deductions your signed proof of delivery disproves, and promo allowances above what was agreed.
reaches_the_model: When an assistant calls a tool, its model sees the result: totals, findings, amounts, quantities, dates, rates, SKUs, order, listing and tracking numbers and finding codes in clear, and text such as product titles, campaign names, seller names, and return and cancel reasons exactly as they were typed. Shopper names and e-mails become stable pseudonyms such as CUS-3f9a2c1b, staff names STAFF-…, affiliate names AFF-…, street addresses [ADDRESS], phone numbers [PHONE] and card numbers [CARD] (checked in the 9 agents that read personal data with 58 planted fictional values: 0 leaks). Free text is sent as typed unless it contains a name already read from a personal column. The report and draft files written on your computer keep the real values. Results go to whatever model your assistant uses; for shopper or staff data, use a model covered by your own agreements or a local model.
rules_maintained: Every rule that changes with a marketplace, carrier, processor or state is a setting, not code: fee schedules, FBA storage rates and aged-inventory brackets, sales tax rates and registrations, nexus thresholds, reserve terms, MAP lists, affiliate and 3PL rates, payout timing and claim windows. Most ship with no real value at all (the demo values are fictional); a few have a built-in default that mirrors a vendor rule as of November 2026 (FBA claim windows, the dimensional weight divisor, carrier dispute and label refund windows), listed with where each lives in docs/rules-2026-11-19.md. Your own values go in each agent's settings file, and every result names the settings files it used. You change the file yourself, or support updates it when a vendor or state announces a change.
